Package game.crow

Class Perching

java.lang.Object
game.creaturestate.BaseCreatureState
game.crow.Perching
All Implemented Interfaces:
CreatureState
public class Perching extends BaseCreatureState
The crow's default, idle state: wanders aimlessly around the map, watching for food or for actors to mob. Its ordinary turn builds a fresh WanderBehaviour using the crow's own randomness, queried through its RandomnessSource capability -- this state must stay constructible with no arguments (a new instance is created on every transition), so it cannot hold a pre-built WanderBehaviour of its own.

From here the crow moves to Mobbing if exactly one actor is nearby, or to Foraging once food comes within sensing range; otherwise it stays perching. Mobbing and Fleeing both settle back into this state once their own conditions for leaving are met.

      public Perching()
      Creates this state. A new instance is created every time a transition returns this state; BaseCreatureState gives every instance of the same class the same identity, so creating a fresh one each time costs nothing.

    • nextState

      public CreatureState nextState(Actor creature, GameMap map)
      Moves to Mobbing if exactly one other actor is visible within sensing range and it is carrying something (a lone target worth harassing). Moves to Foraging once food is visible within sensing range. Otherwise stays perching.

      Mobbing is checked first: if a lone actor is nearby the crow prioritises the confrontation over scavenging for food.

      Parameters:
      creature - the crow whose next state is being decided
      map - the map the crow is on
      Returns:
      the next state
